```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(EasySILAC)
```

## Simulate a heavy-ratio time course

```{r}
set.seed(1)
t <- rep(c(1, 2, 4, 6), each = 4)
k_true <- 0.25
ratio <- 1 - 0.95 * exp(-k_true * t)
ratio_obs <- pmin(pmax(ratio + rnorm(length(t), 0, 0.02), 0.001), 0.999)
total_obs <- 100 * (1 + 0.02 * t) + rnorm(length(t), 0, 2)
```

## Steady-state fit (R engine)

```{r}
fit_silac(ratio = ratio_obs, t = t, Peptide = "toy_protein", total = total_obs)
```

## Steady-state fit (Rust engine)

Requires `rextendr` and a Rust toolchain; compiled once per machine.

```{r eval = requireNamespace("rextendr", quietly = TRUE)}
fit_silac_rust(ratio = ratio_obs, t = t, Peptide = "toy_protein", total = total_obs)
```

## Non-steady-state fit

```{r}
fit_silac_nonsteady(ratio = ratio_obs, total = total_obs, t = t, Peptide = "toy_protein")
```

## Switch engines globally

```{r eval = requireNamespace("rextendr", quietly = TRUE)}
silac_use_rust(TRUE)
fit_silac(ratio = ratio_obs, t = t, Peptide = "toy_protein", total = total_obs)
silac_use_rust(FALSE)
```

## Global labeling-efficiency (Hill) correction

Given mean heavy ratios per sample (H100/H75/H50) and time point, fit the
efficiency curve `E(x) = x^h / (K^h + x^h)`:

```{r eval = FALSE}
hill <- fit_hill_labelling_efficiency(global_full_ratio)
hill$K; hill$h; hill$lambda
hill$plots$p_collapse  # corrected ratios collapse onto one curve
```
